decisional-dimension-tradeoff: People who prioritise their own shape most strongly in the perceptual task prioritise it least when judging whose shape it is.
hypothesis-capacity-mechanism-not-weight: Linking a shape to the self raises total processing capacity rather than just shifting attentional weight between the shapes.
hypothesis-self-association-alters-atten: Arbitrarily pairing a shape with the self speeds how fast that shape is selected into awareness, with no social judgement needed.
hypothesis-social-perceptual-independent: Social salience and perceptual salience capture attention through independent mechanisms, so their effects simply add up.
interprets-bundesen-tva-framework: Bundesen's Theory of Visual Attention splits attention into a total processing capacity and relative weights on each stimulus.
other-association-advantage-social-condi: In the second experiment's social decision task, the other-associated shape was processed faster than the self-associated one.
perceptual-salience-6hz-advantage: Making a shape higher in local colour contrast speeds its processing and slows the competing shape.
prediction-additive-effects-other-associ: For an other-associated shape that is also high-contrast, the two speed-ups should simply add, with no interaction between them.
prediction-capacity-model-outperforms-we: A TVA model that lets processing capacity change with condition should fit the data better than one holding capacity fixed.
prediction-self-advantage-attenuated-soc: Requiring an explicit judgement of whose shape it is should shrink or reverse the self-advantage seen in the perceptual task.
prediction-self-advantage-perceptual-dec: When asked only which shape flickered first, people should process the self-associated shape faster than the other-associated one.
processing-capacity-rises-perceptual-sel: In the perceptual task, processing capacity rises and the gain goes to the self-associated shape, not the other-associated one.
scope-toj-tva-paradigm: All claims rest on two preregistered online experiments using temporal order judgements of arbitrarily self-paired shapes.
self-prioritization-absent-social-decisi: When the task is to report whose shape flickered first, the self-associated shape holds no processing advantage.
self-prioritization-automatic-early: Self-association speeds attentional selection automatically and early, before any decoding of social identity.
self-prioritization-perceptual-decision-: Asked only which shape flickered first, people processed the self-associated shape faster than the other-associated one.
self-salience-dominates-other-associated: Social salience drives attention more for self-associated shapes, physical salience more for other-associated ones.
self-salience-reduces-perceptual-benefit: A self-associated shape gains less from being made perceptually salient than an other-associated or unassociated shape does.
self-social-additive-perceptual: For other-associated shapes, the social and the perceptual speed-up add up with no interaction between them.
social-perceptual-salience-independent-s: Social and perceptual salience capture attention through separate processing streams rather than drawing on one shared resource.
spe-matching-correlates-social-decision: Self-prioritisation in the matching task tracks processing gains in the social decision task but not in the perceptual one.
spe-robust-matching-both-experiments: Participants in both experiments matched the self-associated shape faster, confirming they had learned the shape-person pairings.
tva-capacity-model-wins: A TVA model whose processing capacity is free to change between conditions fits better than one holding capacity fixed.
